what_this_is: Real `validate-intent --version` and `--schema-source` output, captured byte for byte from binaries built for the purpose. Nothing here is hand-written: the parse this gem performs on the --schema-source surface degrades silently by design (any output it cannot read is indistinguishable from a binary too old to have the flag), so a fixture written to fit the pattern would go green on both sides of a parse bug.

how: SchemaPath() is <dir of exe>/../schemas/open-test-intent.v1.json, so each case is a tree: <case>/bin/validate-intent, optionally <case>/schemas/open-test-intent.v1.json.
embedded:      no schemas/ beside the binary.
on_disk:       schemas/open-test-intent.v1.json = a copy of this gem's vendored schema, under a directory whose name contains a space.

disk_wins:     schemas/open-test-intent.v1.json = the vendored schema with its `title` set to "OpenTestIntent v1 (altered on disk)", so it loads and digests differently. The alteration is DIFFERENT from embed_differs' on purpose: the two cases must not share a digest, or a reader cannot tell which one a failure is about. Both are spelled out here so a re-recording reproduces these exact digests rather than merely similar ones.

embed_differs: built with open-test-intent's own schemas/open-test-intent.v1.json altered to `title` "OpenTestIntent v1 (altered embed)" (restored immediately after, which is why the identity carries -dirty), with the vendored schema on disk beside it.

unsupported:   built from an archive of cd8753b, the commit before --schema-source landed, with this gem's vendored schema swapped in before building. The swap is load-bearing: the case asserts contract :matched, which requires the CARRIED digest to be the gem's, and cd8753b predates the current schema. Built without VCS metadata, hence the `unknown` identity.
unloadable:    schemas/open-test-intent.v1.json = the ten bytes `{ not json`.

embedded.what: No schema file beside the binary, so the loader falls back to the compiled-in copy. Origin is the literal <embedded schema>; carried and enforced digests agree.

on_disk.what: A schema file beside the binary, at a path containing a SPACE, holding the same bytes the gem vendors. Proves the origin is not a single token.

disk_wins.what: THE CASE THIS TICKET EXISTS FOR. The compiled-in schema is the one the gem vendors -- --version's digest MATCHES -- while a different schema beside the binary is what a run would load. The carried digest says everything is fine; the enforced digest is not ours.

embed_differs.what: THE MIRROR. Built from a modified schema, so --version carries a digest the gem does not vendor, while the schema beside it IS the gem's. Comparing the carried digest refuses a run that is correct.

unsupported.what: A binary predating open-test-intent slice 19 (built at cd8753b, one commit before --schema-source landed). It reads the flag as a filename.

unloadable.what: A schema that exists beside the binary and is not JSON. --schema-source runs the real loader, so it fails exactly as a verdict run would: exit 2 with the could-not-load diagnostic.
